ticket.title: Cache balance lookups for 60 seconds
ticket.why: `GET /v1/reports/balance` recomputes the balance view on every call. Dashboards poll it every few seconds and the store shows it as the most expensive query by a wide margin.
ticket.what: Read `balance(period)` through the storage layer's TTL cache (`src/ledger/storage/cache.py`) keyed by tenant and period with a 60 s TTL. Writes already invalidate the cache through `post_entry`, so no invalidation code is needed in the reports service.
acceptance: Two `balance(period)` calls within 60 s hit the store once.
A `post_entry` for the same tenant makes the next `balance(period)` call hit the store again.
The cached value equals the uncached value.

file.patch:
diff --git a/src/ledger/services/reports.py b/src/ledger/services/reports.py
index 5c1a2f0..9e7d3b4 100644
--- a/src/ledger/services/reports.py
+++ b/src/ledger/services/reports.py
@@ -1,12 +1,23 @@
 """Reporting service: balances and trial balances from the reporting views."""
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import time
+
 from ledger.storage import views
 from ledger.types import BalanceReport, Period
 
+_BALANCE_TTL_S = 60.0
+_balance_cache: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[float, BalanceReport]] = {}
+
 
 def balance(period: Period) -> BalanceReport:
     """The tenant balance for ``period`` from the reporting view."""
+    key = (period.tenant_id, period.id)
+    hit = _balance_cache.get(key)
+    if hit is not None and time.monotonic() - hit[0] < _BALANCE_TTL_S:
+        return hit[1]
     rows = views.balance(period)
     total = sum(row.amount_minor for row in rows)
-    return BalanceReport(period_id=period.id, balance=total, currency=period.currency)
+    report = BalanceReport(period_id=period.id, balance=total, currency=period.currency)
+    _balance_cache[key] = (time.monotonic(), report)
+    return report

rules.text: Interface code never calls the store directly; it goes through a service.
Every write to the ledger goes through `post_entry`, which enforces double entry.
The storage layer is the only layer that contains SQL.
Cross-cutting side effects (audit, email) are published on the event bus, not called inline.
Reports read from the reporting views, never from the entries table.
Money is handled as integer minor units; a float never reaches the storage layer.

conventions.text: Public functions in production modules carry type hints and a one-line docstring; test functions in `test_*.py` are exempt.
Errors are raised as `LedgerError` subclasses; handlers translate them, services never catch broadly.
Tests live next to the module they cover as `test_<module>.py` and run with pytest.
Commit messages are imperative and under 72 characters on the first line.
Log lines are structured key=value pairs, never f-strings with embedded values.

components.name: API router
components.provides: Maps HTTP routes to service calls and turns service errors into JSON error responses.

components.name: Auth
components.provides: Session cookie and API token authentication as router middleware; loads the current tenant.

components.name: Cache helper
components.provides: A TTL cache in front of Postgres store reads, keyed by query name and parameters, invalidated on every write through post_entry.
components.interface: get(key) -> value | None; set(key, value, ttl_s=60); invalidate(prefix)

components.name: CSV importer
components.provides: Parses bank statement CSV files into candidate entries and posts them through post_entry after matching rules.

components.name: Event bus
components.provides: An in-process publish/subscribe bus for audit, email and webhook side effects, drained after each request.

components.name: Invoice renderer
components.provides: Renders invoices to HTML and PDF from a period's entries using server-side templates.

components.name: Ledger CLI
components.provides: Command-line entry point for posting entries, closing periods and running imports against a local or remote Ledger.

components.name: Postgres store
components.provides: All SQL for entries, periods, tenants and reporting views; the only module that opens a database connection.
